findings.claim: Todo.to_dict() reads `done` twice without the store lock: once in asdict(self), again in is_overdue(). POST /todos calls it after TodoStore.create() has released the lock. A concurrent POST /todos/{id}/complete for the new id can flip done between the two reads, so the POST response says done=false, overdue=false for a past-due todo. That contradicts the Todo response object rule (overdue iff done is false and due_date < today). list_dicts avoids this by building dicts under the lock (app/storage.py:43, whose comment states that intent), but the single-object paths were left out.

evidence.reproduction: git clone /workspace/repo /tmp/r && cd /tmp/r && git checkout 1ad4332 && PYTHONPATH=. python /mnt/session/outputs/probes/probe_race_post_response.py   # part A runs store.create('race', date(2000,1,1)).to_dict() (exactly what app/main.py:50 does) against a thread spinning store.complete(next_id) (what the complete route does), with sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6) to widen the window
evidence.observed: torn response example: {'id': 1, 'title': 'race', 'done': False, 'created_at': '2026-10-10T12:22:30.733091+00:00', 'due_date': '2000-01-01', 'overdue': False}; part A: 49 torn responses in 20000 rounds (32/20000 in an earlier run). Over HTTP with the default switch interval (part B, 1500 rounds) I did not hit it, so in practice the window is narrow. It also needs a client that completes an id it has not yet been given.
evidence.expected: Every todo response is internally consistent: overdue == (not done and due_date is not None and due_date < today). With a single snapshot in to_dict, part A gives 0 torn responses in 20000 (checked on a scratch copy outside the repo; 37 tests still pass).

violates: interfaces['Todo response object']: overdue true iff done is false AND due_date is not null AND due_date < today_utc()
goal: 'missed if any flag disagrees with the rule'
findings.refutation_condition: I withdraw this if either holds. (a) Code shows that `done` cannot change between asdict(self) and is_overdue(): to_dict derives overdue from the asdict snapshot, or the POST/complete routes build their dict while holding TodoStore._lock, and probe_race_post_response.py part A then reports 0 torn responses in 20000 rounds. (b) The spec owner states that single-object responses need not be consistent under concurrent writes to the same todo.
findings.suggested_fix: In Todo.to_dict, take d = asdict(self) once and compute d['overdue'] from d['done'] and d['due_date'] (with today defaulting to today_utc()). Alternatively, have create/complete return the dict built under the lock. Either keeps the interface signatures the spec gives.

findings.claim: Intermediate commit d33b244 declares `due_date: date | None = None`. At that commit POST /todos accepts '2026-11-30T00:00:00' and 0 and stores them as '2026-11-30' and '1970-01-01', which is exactly what AC-9 forbids. The slice still passes its test plan only because that commit's tests do not exercise AC-9. The history was deliberately rebuilt as slices meant to stand alone, so a non-squash merge leaves a commit on main where a bisect or partial revert gives a service that stores malformed due dates. The merged tree at 1ad4332 is not affected.
